statement.zh: Frankfurt/JAA 年代学将诺克文化工作年代置于约 1500 BCE 至公元纪元初（Breunig/Rupp 等）。
statement.en: Frankfurt/JAA chronologies place the Nok culture working span ca. 1500 BCE to the turn of the Common Era (Breunig/Rupp et al.).

statement.zh: Fagg 识别传统与其后目录将特色陶俑雕塑作为诺克物质文化核心标志（Fagg；博物馆目录传统）。
statement.en: Fagg’s identification tradition and later catalogs treat distinctive terracotta sculpture as a core Nok material-culture marker (Fagg; museum catalog tradition).

statement.zh: 研究讨论诺克语境中的早期冶铁证据，并与塔鲁加等地联系起来（JAA；冶铁专文）。
statement.en: Research discusses early iron-smelting evidence in Nok contexts and links it to localities such as Taruga (JAA; iron-technology papers).

statement.zh: Frankfurt 项目报告将萨蒙·杜基亚等地点作为发掘的定居/陶俑语境（JAA outline）。
statement.en: Frankfurt project reports treat localities such as Samun Dukiya as excavated settlement/terracotta contexts (JAA outline).

statement.zh: 考古传统以乔斯高原及周边作为诺克文化命名类型区（Fagg；JAA）。
statement.en: Archaeological tradition treats the Jos Plateau and surroundings as the Nok name-giving type region (Fagg; JAA).

statement.zh: 研究史将杰马与著名陶俑头像发现及测年讨论相联系（Fagg 传统）。
statement.en: Research history links Jemaa with the famous terracotta head discovery and dating discussions (Fagg tradition).

statement.zh: 更广的西非早期铁器综述将诺克置于区域「铁器化」讨论中（手册取向）。
statement.en: Broader West African early-iron syntheses place Nok within regional ironization debates (handbook orientation).

statement.zh: 假说：依据陶俑与冶铁推断「国家」或等级社会复杂度的模型仍证据不足，宜保持考古文化表述（JAA 讨论语境）。
statement.en: Hypothesis: inferring ‘state’ or ranked social complexity from terracottas and iron remains underdetermined; prefer archaeological-culture wording (JAA discussion context).

claims.disclaimer: Hypothesis: political-complexity inferences are debated; not established fact.

statement.zh: 尼日利亚博物馆与国际馆藏目录构成诺克陶俑风格研究的主要组合来源之一（目录传统；T 级公开展示需降权）。
statement.en: Nigerian museum and international catalogs form a major assemblage source for Nok terracotta style studies (catalog tradition; public displays remain tier T).

statement.zh: 《Archaeology》等公共综述仅作大众导向，不能替代发掘报告（tier T）。
statement.en: Public magazine overviews such as Archaeology Magazine are orientation-only and do not replace excavation reports (tier T).
